title: HomeFlood Notice, Renewal and Cancellation Periods Schedule
content:
**HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies** — servicing periods and refund terms by tier. Day counts are calendar days.

| Tier | Nonpayment notice period (days) | Notice before Tidemark cancels for another reason or non-renews (days) | Renewal offer issued before term end (days) | Reinstatement window after expiration (days) | Refund method on the insured's cancellation | Policy fee refundable on cancellation | Term with a paid claim earns its full premium |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HomeFlood Renters | 10 | 45 | 60 | 30 | pro rata | no | yes |
| HomeFlood Essential | 45 | 45 | 60 | 30 | pro rata | no | yes |
| HomeFlood Standard | 45 | 45 | 60 | 30 | pro rata | no | yes |
| HomeFlood Plus | 45 | 45 | 60 | 30 | pro rata | no | yes |
| HomeFlood Premier | 45 | 45 | 60 | 30 | pro rata | no | yes |
| HomeFlood Estate | 45 | 45 | 60 | 30 | pro rata | no | yes |

## Notes to the schedule

- The **nonpayment notice period** runs from the date a notice of cancellation for nonpayment is issued to the cancellation date it states. HomeFlood Renters gives 10 days; every other tier gives 45.
- The **45-day notice** is the written notice to the insured and the mortgagee before Tidemark cancels for any reason other than nonpayment, or non-renews.
- The **renewal offer** goes out 60 days before term end.
- The **reinstatement window** is the 30 days after expiration within which an unpaid renewal can be reinstated on a signed statement of no loss.
- The **refund method** on the insured's cancellation is pro rata on every tier. The policy fee is not refundable, and a term with a paid claim earns its full premium on cancellation.

*Hypothetical illustration:* a HomeFlood Renters nonpayment notice issued on the 1st of a 30-day month states a cancellation date of the 11th; the same notice on a HomeFlood Plus policy states the 16th of the following month.
